findings.title: Reverse causation and unmeasured confounding by cancer history/frailty
findings.mechanism: The study did not exclude or match on prior history of breast cancer or baseline comorbidities. Clinicians are less likely to initiate GLP-1 receptor agonists in patients with active malignancy, prior cancer history, or unexplained weight loss/frailty, while healthier patients receive GLP-1s.
findings.direction: Pushes the estimate toward an artificial protective effect (lower OR for GLP-1), as evidenced by the lower baseline event rate in the GLP-1 group.

findings.title: Biologically implausible latency and exposure misclassification
findings.mechanism: Exposure required only a single prior or current prescription with no minimum duration, dose, or washout, over an observational window of at most 3.5 years (Jan 2022 – Jun 2025). Solid tumor development takes years; a true biological chemopreventive effect cannot materialize almost immediately after any exposure, indicating the observed difference stems from baseline selection rather than drug action.
findings.direction: Spuriously favors GLP-1 as protective against breast cancer.

findings.title: Lack of time-to-event analysis and survival/immortal time bias
findings.mechanism: Using standard logistic regression rather than survival analysis (time-to-event) ignores differential person-time at risk, loss to follow-up, censoring, and potential immortal time between cohort entry and first prescription.
findings.direction: Biases odds ratios downward (favoring GLP-1) if exposed person-time accrued before event-free status was guaranteed.
evidence: Логистическая регрессия, оценка через odds ratio

findings.title: Potential collider/selection bias from matching on maximum BMI and conditioning on mammography
findings.mechanism: All patients were selected conditionally on having undergone mammography, but screening frequency was not balanced. Furthermore, matching on 'maximum BMI' rather than baseline BMI or trajectory may adjust for post-baseline or intermediate variables affected by treatment.
findings.direction: Distorts the true association; controls with same max BMI may have had different weight trajectories or screening intensities.

extra_findings.title: Biologically implausible latency period
extra_findings.why: A maximum observation period of 3.5 years is biologically too short for a pharmacological chemopreventive effect on de novo solid tumor incidence, reinforcing that the observed association is driven by baseline selection.

verdict.notes: The auditor correctly classified the study and computed the exact absolute metrics, but fell into the healthy-user trap regarding comorbidity gradient.

findings.title: Baseline history of breast cancer imbalance (prevalent cancer / recurrence confounding)
findings.mechanism: Patients with prior breast cancer have a significantly higher risk of a subsequent or recurrent breast cancer diagnosis. The control group had a higher prevalence of prior breast cancer at baseline than the GLP-1 group, which directly inflates the event rate in the control group.
findings.direction: Biases the odds ratio downwards (spurious protective effect for GLP-1), because the control group had a higher baseline rate of prior breast cancer (7.8% vs 5.9% in the matched cohort; 9.2% vs 5.9% in the full cohort).
evidence: Personal history of breast cancer in full cohort: Control 9.2% (8,876) vs GLP-1 5.9% (907)
Personal history of breast cancer in matched cohort: Control 7.8% vs GLP-1 5.9%
Matching was explicitly not performed on breast cancer history

findings.title: Improper exposure definition and immortal time / latency bias
findings.mechanism: Defining exposure as 'any prior or current use' without minimum duration, dose, washout period, or time-to-event analysis violates biological plausibility for oncogenesis (which requires years of latency) and introduces immortal time/prevalent user biases. Furthermore, logistic regression without time-to-event ignores differences in follow-up time.
findings.direction: Unclear overall theoretical direction, but in short observation windows (Jan 2022 - Jun 2025 = 3.5 years max), acute/recent initiators cannot biologically experience cancer prevention; early events in users may be prevalent or cause reverse causality.

Study observation period: 2022-01-01 to 2025-06-30 (maximum 3.5 years)

findings.title: Selection bias from conditioning on mammography screening
findings.mechanism: Restricting the cohort only to women who received a mammogram (217,624 selected) conditions on healthcare-seeking behavior and screening indication. If GLP-1 users undergo mammography for different reasons or at different frequencies than non-users, detection rates will be systematically biased.

findings.title: Competing risks and unadjusted comorbidity imbalance
findings.mechanism: The GLP-1 cohort has substantially higher severe comorbidity (Charlson index ≥ 5, cardiac, and renal disease). In a logistic regression without accounting for competing risks of mortality or differential clinical surveillance, higher non-cancer morbidity/mortality can artificially reduce observed cancer diagnoses.
findings.direction: Pushes the estimate toward a protective effect (lower odds of breast cancer diagnosis in GLP-1 group due to competing clinical priorities/events).
